questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Being able to experience a foreign university and culture and living abroad for a while.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Both USYD and KU provided all the necessary information on the respective websites. In case of doubt, my Australian coordinator replied quite fast to upfront questions. After being nominated it took very long until I heard back from USYD and the whole enrolment from Sydney took long which made it a bit stressful with the visa.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were lots of information meetings in the orientation week before lectures began, including one with our coordinator and USYD made sure that we got all the necessary information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I decided against student accommodation because most of them are far more expensive than private flatshares. I recommend to book an accommodation/ hostel upon arriving and going to viewings while in the city. I found my room on facebook, where there are several groups to find rooms. There is also an app called flatmates but from my experience, the shared houses on facebook were more personal.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living costs are quite expensive in Sydney and I would suggest living close to the campus as there are lots of leisure activities like clubs and sports and many classes are mandatory.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The "guaranteed housing" from the university means you need to be very very quick in order to get a spot at more affordable student housing or else you need to pay a lot for private student housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There is a course catalogue for all the courses available but it is very long and a bit overwhelming to look through all of it. You can apply for more courses than you actually need to take which gives more flexibility. There are some courses my coordinator could approve right away and others needed faculty approval which took very long.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Course catalogue with courses for exchange students and the USYD webpage with all the courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Some of the courses I registered for were not available anymore and I had to change 2 courses. Apart from that I got in all the courses I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to look through all of the USYD webpage even though it can be overwhelming and don't stress if your courses aren't approved yet, it took a while for mine to be approved by the faculty.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of my courses was lower than compared to KU but workload was higher, there were lots of group presentations and other assignments throughout the semester. Additionally, I had 4 courses and 3 exams at the same time, so the study period was a bit more intense.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some of my classes were more interactive and the relation to the professors was closer than at KU. Other classes were way larger and felt more anonymous than at KU. Most of my lectures were recorded and tutorials required attendance.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Behavioural Economics
Market Structure and Strategic Behaviour
Logistics and Future Cities
Energy and Resources

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really enjoyed Energy and Resources because the professor was very motivated and it dealt with many relevant topics. I learned a lot during the course because in the tutorials, we always had to deep dive on the lecture's content and present something.
Behavioural Economics was very interesting topic-wise but I didn't like the teaching style, so I always rewatched the lecture videos.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None. I went travelling as much as I could which is of course expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: USYD has lots of affordable food options, e.g. a food hub where you can get 3 food items for free each day or the coffee happy hour where coffee is half the price during a certain time a day or the 5 $ meal.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: USYD has a lot of different clubs students can join. I joined the surf society and uni gym.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The surf society never went surfing but they had nice socials at the beginning to meet friends. Apart from that just talk to the members in o-week and join the groups you find most interesting.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Try to travel as much as you can, from Sydney you can take the train to the blue mountains or to Wollongong or New Castle. I also travelled to Tasmania, Melbourne, the Great Ocean Road and did a road trip on both East and West Coast, the possibilities are honestly endless and everything is so nice. In the easter holidays, I went to K'gari Island, which was one of my highlights.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, everyone is really friendly and laid back.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didn't socialise that much with fellow students, but I guess you can be lucky in your group works.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There weren't any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The coffee culture, you can find good coffee everywhere and just the open-mindedness of Aussies, their activeness and outdoorsieness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Say yes to everything that sounds fun and don't worry that much about uni and just explore as much as you can. Sydney has lots of free events you can visit. Be brave and talk to people, they always react very warm and friendly.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Inform yourself about all the USYD events, as there are soo many (free) ones.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The amazing people I met and all the travels I did.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Handling the different classes and exams at once in the final exam week but that was very doable.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
